notes: Acceptance criteria for the CRM-Scale release, written as product tickets. Amounts use the workspace currency (USD by default). 'Today' in this product is 15 November 2026.

requirements.criterion: Each role (admin, manager, sales, support, viewer) can sign in with valid credentials and lands on the dashboard showing who is signed in.
A wrong password or an unknown email shows 'Invalid email or password' and the user stays on the login page.
Signing out returns the user to the login page.
API requests without a session are refused with 401.
Opening a protected page while signed out redirects to the login page.
A deactivated user cannot sign in and is told 'This account is deactivated'.
For every role, the main navigation enables exactly the sections listed for that role in roleAccess and disables all other sections.
Opening a page the role may not use, directly by URL, shows 'You do not have access to <path>.'

The API enforces the same role access as the navigation: listing leads, quotes, invoices, users, reports and the audit log, and creating leads and opportunities, succeed only for permitted roles and return 403 for everyone else.
Only admins and managers can export accounts. For other roles the Export button is disabled and the export API returns 403.
Only admins can change settings. Managers see settings read-only with the Save button disabled, and the settings API refuses their changes with 403.
Only admins can read the audit log; other roles see permission denied.
Sales users cannot view reports.
Support users cannot delete contacts: no Delete action is shown and the API returns 403.
Viewers cannot change opportunity stages: no stage actions are shown and the API returns 403.
Sales users can create an account with a name and industry; it appears in the list with an 'Account created' confirmation.
An account cannot be created without a name ('Account name is required').
Account names are unique regardless of letter case ('An account with this name already exists').
Searching accounts filters the list by name.
Lists show ten rows per page, with 'Page X of Y · N total' and a way to reach the next page.
An account with unpaid invoices cannot be deleted ('Account has unpaid invoices and cannot be deleted') and stays in the list.
Admins can delete an account that has no invoices; only admins see the Delete action.
Exporting accounts confirms how many accounts were exported.
Viewers see accounts read-only, with a read-only banner and no New account action.
Support users can create a contact with a name and email.
A contact needs a valid email address ('A valid email is required').
Managers can delete a contact after confirming, and it leaves the list.
Contact search matches either the contact's name or their email.
Sales users can create a lead; new leads have status 'open'.
Lead name, email and source are each required.
A lead email must be a valid address ('Enter a valid email address').
A lead email may not match an existing lead, ignoring case ('A lead with this email already exists').
Converting a lead that has a company creates a contact and an account, and marks the lead 'converted'.
Converting a lead without a company creates a contact only, no account.
A converted lead cannot be converted again: the API refuses with 409 'Lead is already converted' and the list no longer offers Convert.
Managers can convert leads but cannot create them.
Each stage carries a fixed probability (prospecting 10%, qualification 25%, proposal 50%, negotiation 75%, won 100%, lost 0%) and weighted value is value × probability.
New opportunities start in prospecting.
Opportunity value must be a positive number; zero and negative values are rejected.
An opportunity must belong to an account ('Choose an account').
Advancing an opportunity moves it to the next stage.
Marking an opportunity won sets its probability to 100%.
Closing an opportunity as lost requires a reason.
The reason given when closing as lost is stored on the opportunity.
Quote totals: subtotal is the sum of quantity × unit price, the discount applies to the subtotal, tax is 18% of the discounted subtotal, and the total is rounded half up to two decimals.
A discount above the approval threshold (15% by default) puts the quote into 'pending-approval'; a discount exactly at the threshold does not.
The approval threshold follows the workspace setting, and the quotes page states the current threshold.
Only managers and admins can approve quotes; sales users see no Approve action and the API returns 403.
Approving a pending quote returns it to 'draft' so it can be sent.
A quote pending approval cannot be sent ('Quote needs approval before it can be sent') and keeps its status.
A sent quote can be marked accepted.
Discounts above 50% are rejected.
Every quote line needs an item, a quantity above zero and a price.
An invoice created from an accepted quote gets the next sequential number in the form INV-2026-NNNN and starts as 'draft' with the quote total as its balance.
Only accepted quotes can be invoiced ('Only accepted quotes can be invoiced').
A draft invoice can be sent.
A payment below the balance marks the invoice 'partially-paid' and leaves the remaining balance.
Paying the full balance marks the invoice 'paid' with a zero balance.
A payment above the balance is rejected.
Payments cannot be recorded on a draft invoice.
An unpaid invoice past its due date is flagged overdue; a paid invoice is never overdue.
Support users can view invoices but cannot create them.
A new invoice is due 30 days after it is issued.
Tasks are listed by due date, earliest first, including newly added tasks.
Open tasks past their due date are flagged overdue; completed tasks never are.
A task needs a title and a due date.
Only a task's assignee or an admin can complete it; others are told 'Only the assignee or an admin can complete this task'.
Viewers cannot add tasks.
Open pipeline sums the value of opportunities that are neither won nor lost, and drops a deal once it is won.
Weighted pipeline sums value × stage probability over open opportunities.
'Won this quarter' sums deals won since 1 October 2026.
Outstanding invoices sum the remaining balances of unpaid invoices, not their full totals.
Reports count open tasks that are overdue.
Admins can invite a user by email; the email must be valid and not already belong to a user.
An invited user receives the role chosen in the invitation.
Admins can change a user's role.
The last active admin cannot be demoted to another role ('The workspace must keep at least one active admin').
The last active admin cannot be deactivated.
Admins can change the approval threshold to a value between 0 and 50%.
Changing the currency changes how amounts are displayed.
Creating a lead is recorded in the audit log.
Deleting an account or a contact is recorded in the audit log.
Deleting a lead is recorded in the audit log.
Changes to settings are recorded in the audit log.
The dashboard tells each user how many of their own tasks are overdue.
Overdue work is easy to spot.
Forms handle invalid input gracefully.
Reports load quickly enough for managers to use them in meetings.
Amounts are shown consistently in the workspace currency across the product.
Sales users understand when a quote will need approval before they submit it.
